rockyHillNorth.sponsorExperience: Dale Development is a family run, vertically integrated multifamily developer with more than twenty years of experience building suburban apartment communities across the Northeast. The firm was founded by Brendan Dale's father, who began his career at Toll Brothers before building a track record of projects in New Jersey, Connecticut and Westchester County, New York, with Rocky Hill North marking its first project in Massachusetts. Dale Development typically develops communities in high barrier to entry suburban submarkets with limited new supply, managing the full lifecycle from land entitlement and capital formation through construction, lease up and sale, and has partnered with institutional capital including Starwood, Clarion Partners and Harbor Group on prior developments. The firm secured favorable zoning, state environmental approval and state grant funding for this site and maintains a long standing relationship with JLL's Boston capital markets team.
rockyHillNorth.summary: The sponsor is developing the project from the ground up, delivering an elevator served, walk up and stacked townhome community arranged in a walkable New England village layout that will offer the newest and highest quality rental product the submarket has seen in years. The resident base is expected to be drawn from renters priced out of local homeownership as well as those renting by choice, including professionals working in the surrounding technology, medical and life science employment corridors. The community will feature an extensive amenity package anchored by a clubhouse with coworking space, a recreation fieldhouse with a full fitness center, a pool with cabanas, indoor and outdoor pickleball and basketball courts, and expansive green space and walking trails that distinguish it from the existing competitive set, complemented by a modest affordable component required under the local approvals.

aurea.name: Black Salmon Capital Holdings and The Allen Morris Company | Aurea at Highland Park
aurea.sponsorName: Black Salmon Capital Holdings and The Allen Morris Company
aurea.sponsorExperience: Black Salmon Capital Holdings is a commercial real estate investment and development firm headquartered in Coral Gables, Florida, focused on residential, industrial, hospitality and mixed use opportunities across the United States, often employing a long term land assembly strategy to secure attractive development basis in core urban submarkets. The Allen Morris Company, founded in 1958 and also based in Coral Gables with a regional office in Atlanta, is a multi generational, family owned developer of mixed use, residential, commercial and hotel projects across the Southeast. Black Salmon has assembled an acquisition and development portfolio spanning major metropolitan areas including Austin, Atlanta, Miami, Orlando, Phoenix and San Francisco, with a large development pipeline in South Florida. The Allen Morris Company has completed more than 5.6 million square feet of commercial and residential projects since inception, with a senior leadership team carrying over 100 years of combined development experience.
aurea.summary: Aurea at Highland Park sits at the gateway of Miami's urban core, offering direct access to downtown, the airport and I-95 via SR 836, with the Culmer Metrorail stop within walking distance and Miami Central Station a few stops north. Designed by Arquitectonica, the high rise multifamily tower includes a rooftop pool overlooking the downtown Miami skyline and sits within walking distance of the Miami Health District, the second largest health district in the country, anchored by Jackson Memorial Hospital, the University of Miami Health System, Bascom Palmer Eye Institute and the new Ken Griffin Cancer Research Center, whose large employee and visitor base currently lacks a dedicated multifamily option nearby. The property also sits near the newly announced Carnegie Mellon Miami campus in Wynwood, a graduate focused campus funded in part by a major philanthropic gift from Ken Griffin and expected to bring a new base of high income renter demand to the surrounding submarket. Aurea is the first phase of Highland Park Miami, a multi phase transit oriented district being planned as a live, work and play environment with linear parks, service retail and future residential, hotel and flex uses. With financing conditions slowing new construction starts across the broader market, the project is positioned to deliver into a period of limited competing supply and strong rental growth potential, while also standing to benefit from Florida's Live Local Act entitlements and potential future opportunity zone designation.
